rounds.fact: Digital Trends grew as a general consumer-electronics review site during the mid-2000s, competing for readers alongside CNET and Engadget in a crowded gadget-blog era.
MSN launched alongside Windows 95 as Microsoft's answer to AOL, bundling a dial-up service with a portal homepage that shipped as the default for millions of new PCs.
Opera was one of the first browsers to introduce tabbed browsing and built-in mouse gestures, features that later became standard across every major browser.
BuzzFeed started in 2006 as an experiment in tracking what content spreads virally online, well before its listicle format became one of the most imitated web formats of the 2010s.
TMZ launched in 2005 and dramatically sped up the celebrity news cycle, frequently breaking major stories hours or days before traditional entertainment outlets.
